hypothesis: Broad Indian asset-class ETFs that have risen over the last ~3 months and trade above their ~5-month average tend to keep outperforming over the following weeks, and stepping aside when trends break reduces losses. This is a modest, well-documented effect; it is NOT expected to come anywhere near 10% per day.
rules_plain_english: After each close, for every ETF compute (a) its 63-session price change and (b) whether it closed above its 100-session simple average. Prices are adjusted for splits, bonuses and dividends.
An ETF is eligible only if it is above its average AND its 63-session change is positive.
Every 5th session of the experiment (sessions 1, 6, 11, 16), hold the top 2 eligible ETFs by 63-session change. If fewer than 2 qualify, the unused slots stay in cash. If none qualify, hold nothing.
On any session, if a held ETF closed below its 100-session average the previous day, sell it at the next session.
Signals use closes up to and including day D and are executed during session D+1 (order sent at 09:20 IST). A close is never used to trade on the same day.
Buy orders are DAY limit orders at 0.5% above the reference price; sells at 3% below (marketable, but protected). Unfilled remainders expire at the close.

Sizing: each slot gets an equal share of the maximum invested amount (Rs12,500 / 2 = Rs6,250), rounded DOWN to whole units after estimated charges. Existing holdings that stay selected are not topped up (avoids small, costly trades).
